what_happened: Precisely isolated and reproduced prune_next_body()'s flag-misparse defect via a standalone awk harness replaying the real function: gsub(/[ \t]/, "", tasklist) fuses a trailing CLI flag onto the last task id (e.g. '714 --hard' -> '714--hard'), which never matches the active-ids lookup. Confirmed four failure shapes incl. the worst case -- total silent disappearance of a single-task flagged Run line (kept=0, n2=1, neither output branch fires). Also found and confirmed an identical sibling defect in count_pruned_next_ids() (jq -e --argjson errors on the fused non-numeric token, exit 2, misread as 'not active'), corrupting the pruned=/retained= stderr diagnostic counters via the same root cause. Confirmed zero existing test coverage of flag-bearing Run lines in either layout's --prune test group.

Research Recommendation 1 proposed splitting the Run line's pre-rationale portion on the first run of whitespace; that would mis-split the grammar-legal '/orchestrate 716, 714 --hard' (the documented Next Grammar admits intra-list spaces via [\d, ]+) into tasklist='716,' and flags='714 --hard', introducing a second content-loss path. The plan narrows the approach to anchor segmentation on the first whitespace-preceded '-' instead, and adds an intra-list-space fixture.

The research report's byte-for-byte reproduction harness and five-input Expected/Actual table let the planning phase skip a dedicated red-baseline phase entirely and write exact-output verification criteria directly, with only a Scope Hypothesis to re-confirm the carried byte-identical-deploy-mirror claim.

covered_ids_from() (roadmap-integration.sh, ~line 523) scrapes all digits from the whole Run line including rationale prose and numeric flag arguments (e.g. --max-tasks 8), mis-attributing them as covered task ids; out of scope for task 388, which only fixes prune_next_body()/count_pruned_next_ids()
git-commit-phase.sh dropped 'specs/388_prune_next_body_flag_misparse_drops_active_task/issues.jsonl' from a phase commit pathspec: not contained in this task's declared file_scope.

Phase 1's fail-safe warning in prune_next_body() embedded a literal single quote inside the awk program's bash single-quoted script delimiter (print "...task id '" bad_id "'..."), which breaks the shell quoting and corrupts the emitted stderr message (observed literal 'bad_id' text instead of the actual id). Not caught by the Phase 1 scratchpad harness because that harness happened to use correct '"'"' escaping when re-typing the function. Caught during Phase 3's full end-to-end --prune run against the real script; fixed by switching the warning's id delimiters from single quotes to square brackets, sidestepping the nested-quoting hazard entirely.

During Phase 5's full gate set (verify-deploy.sh, no narrowing), discovered agent-system/extensions/literature/scripts/tests/test-zotero-generate-export.sh hangs indefinitely -- reproduced in complete isolation with zero contention (timeout 60 against the bare suite: passes one case then stalls past the 60s bound, exit 124). This suite is part of the repository's full tests/run-all.sh sweep (gate 8 of verify-deploy.sh), so ANY full, unnarrowed gate run blocks on it. A concurrent sibling (task 381, on its own final phase doing the same full-gate-plus-redeploy operation) hit the identical hang and its repeated/retried attempts drove system load to 50+ on a 24-core machine. Confirmed unrelated to task 388's three files (roadmap-integration.sh, test-roadmap-generation.sh, roadmap-format.md) via git log and direct inspection -- the literature/zotero extension has zero overlap with roadmap-integration.sh. Closed Phase 5 via a documented Reasoned-Exclusions record naming this and two other pre-existing, confirmed-unrelated verify-deploy.sh findings (a lean-extension doc-lint gap and a 225B eager-load-budget overage) rather than continuing to contend for CPU against the runaway process. Reported to the main/orchestrating session.

verify-deploy.sh's full gate set also surfaced two further pre-existing, confirmed-unrelated-to-task-388 findings: (1) doc-lint FAILs for the lean extension (two test fixture files under scripts/tests/fixtures/challenge/ not registered in provides.scripts) and for project-wide (deployed context/project/lean4/patterns/measurement-harness-strictness.md missing an index.json entry) -- both lean4-domain, zero overlap with roadmap-integration.sh; (2) orchestrator context budget lock: eager-load total 66325 B exceeds the recorded baseline of 66100 B by 225 B -- confirmed via measure-eager-context.sh's own per-file listing that none of task 388's three edited files (roadmap-integration.sh, test-roadmap-generation.sh, roadmap-format.md) are members of the eager-loaded set (only CLAUDE.md, the parent chain, and nine specific rules/*.md files are measured), so this task's edits cannot have caused the overage. Both findings are named in Phase 5's Reasoned Exclusions record rather than fixed here, as neither is in this task's declared scope or file_scope.
